title: MongoDB Introduction
summary: Meet MongoDB, a tool for storing documents. Use a tiny book record to learn what documents, fields and collections mean.
introduction: Imagine a card about a book. It has a title and a page count. MongoDB can store a card like this as a document. A group of documents is called a collection. Start with one book so you can see what each new word means.
learningObjectives: Name the fields in a small document
Add one book to a practice collection
Read the title from a stored book

rows: One record, such as a card about one book.
A named fact inside a document, such as title.

blocks.title: Where to run the examples
blocks.text: Read the [setup lesson](/tutorials/mongodb/setup-atlas-shell) to use MongoDB on your computer. These examples are shown here for reading; they do not run in this site playground.
The braces hold the document. title and pages are fields. The title is text. The page count is a number. This first example just shows the shape of the data.
Type this command in mongosh after selecting your practice database. insertOne adds the document to lessonBooks. MongoDB also gives it a unique _id label.
findOne looks for one document with this title. print shows the title in mongosh. This command reads the document without changing it.

blocks.title: Read the book in mongosh
Watch out
blocks.text: Use a practice database for these commands. Run insertOne once for this example; running it again adds another book. Keep real database passwords out of shared code.

blocks.title: Try one small change
blocks.text: Add a different book title with a page count of 30. Change the findOne question so it finds your new book.
